name: Melkite Schism of 1724
also_known_as: Split of the Patriarchate of Antioch
summary: The division of the Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch into the Greek Orthodox Church and the Melkite Greek Catholic Church, after rival patriarchs were chosen in 1724.

start.label: Rival patriarchs chosen for Antioch: Cyril VI (pro-Rome) and Sylvester

end.label: Rome recognizes Cyril VI as Melkite Catholic patriarch

background.text: Catholic missionaries, especially Jesuits and Capuchins, had been active in Aleppo and Damascus since the 17th century, and a pro-Catholic party had grown among the Arabic-speaking Orthodox of the patriarchate.

happened.text: When Patriarch Athanasios III Dabbas died in 1724, the clergy and people of Damascus elected Cyril VI Tanas, who favored union with Rome.
The Patriarch of Constantinople and his synod instead appointed Sylvester, a Greek monk from Cyprus, as patriarch of Antioch, and obtained Ottoman recognition for him.
Cyril was excommunicated by Constantinople and fled to the Shuwayr monastery in Lebanon; Pope Benedict XIII recognized him in 1729.

participants.name: Cyril VI Tanas
participants.role: First patriarch of the Melkite Greek Catholic Church

participants.name: Sylvester of Antioch
participants.role: Greek Orthodox patriarch appointed from Constantinople

participants.name: Jeremias III
participants.role: Patriarch of Constantinople who backed Sylvester

outcomes.text: Two churches claim the patriarchate of Antioch to this day: the Greek Orthodox Patriarchate of Antioch and the Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarchate.
The Ottoman government recognized the Melkite Catholics as a separate community (millet) only in 1848.
The Greek-dominated hierarchy of the Orthodox patriarchate was replaced by Arab hierarchs in 1899.

condemnations.reason: Cyril VI Tanas excommunicated and declared deposed as a uniate

persecution_note: With Ottoman backing, the Orthodox patriarch's party pressed hard against the Catholic Melkites for over a century.

persecution.title: Pressure on the Catholic Melkites
persecution.summary: Patriarch Sylvester used Ottoman decrees to have Catholic clergy arrested, churches taken, and Catholics forced to accept Orthodox clergy, especially in Aleppo; Catholic Melkites could not legally have their own churches in many cities until the 19th century.

responsible.name: Ottoman authorities
responsible.role: Issued and enforced decrees for the Orthodox patriarch

persecution.outcome: Many Catholics moved to Lebanon; legal recognition came in 1848.

sources.citation: Robert M. Haddad, Syrian Christians in Muslim Society: An Interpretation. Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1970.
